title: Buried Works
text: Home » What lives there » Buried Works The builders who made the ancient cities and the strongholds left one more place behind. You will find it by the hatch.

title: Buried Works
text: Almost nothing shows above ground: a stone hatch under an oak lean-to.

title: Where
text: The Buried Works are the builders' lab, a rare underground structure in the overworld. About as rare as strongholds : roughly one in every 4,000 by 4,000 blocks. The nearest is usually 1,200 to 2,500 blocks away. Only on flat, dry ground, with the ground between y 58 and y 200. Never under water and never in The Remembering. On the surface there is only the hatch : a stone opening under an oak lean-to, with a ladder going down.

title: Finding one
text: A journeyman (level 3) cartographer sells a Buried Works Map for 13 emeralds and a compass , the way they sell the trial chamber map. The map marks the hatch with its own icon . Like the vanilla maps, a cartographer far from any lab does not offer it. /locate structure backrooms:buried_works (vanilla, cheats on) or /backrooms locate works find the nearest one. Going down into one gives the advancement Buried Works .

title: What is inside
text: Below the hatch: a shaft, then stone brick halls like a stronghold's, mossy and cracked. The hub has four doors, all alike. The machine hall is behind one of them, sometimes further on down a hall, round a corner or down a short stair, 33 to about 70 blocks from the hatch. The machine hall holds the builders' last machine in the far wall: a broken Reinforced Iron frame, with the Backrooms pouring out of it: mushroom and mud on the floor, birch on the wall round the frame, sandstone overhead, thinning out into stone brick. The parts are in the chest beside it. The foundry , storerooms left mid-

title: Not craftable
text: Lamps, settled blocks, sherds, the Day One disc, the Settled Heart, the Still Life Head and Memarium ore only come from the world. Remembered Upgrade and Builder Armor Trim templates are found first, then duplicated.

title: FAQ and compatibility
text: Home » Reference » FAQ and compatibility Common questions, every advancement, and how the mod gets on with other mods and servers.

title: How do I get into The Remembering?
text: Repair the broken machine in a Buried Works , or build your own Reinforced Iron frame anywhere and give it a redstone signal. After the first door in a world opens, thin spots can drop you in too.

title: I'm stuck inside. How do I get out?
text: Type /backrooms leave . Or build a door: the chests, barrels and Vivid mobs inside give you iron, copper and redstone.

title: Why don't the blocks drop anything?
text: They are copies. Only blocks you placed, Memarium ore and the vanilla pieces in misremembered places drop normally. A Memarium tool gets a rare drop. See Rules .

title: Why can't I hurt the Keeper?
text: Nothing can until you pin it with the Shape : a Still Life Head on a T of five Blocks of Memarium, built inside The Remembering.

title: Where is the Abyss?
text: It is not in 3.0.0. Under the End floors is the geometric level, and under that the loop brings you back to the top.

title: Is there a lore book?
text: No, on purpose. The story is told only by playing: places, objects, sounds, mob behaviour and the advancements.

title: Immersive Portals
text: Optional. With Immersive Portals installed, every open door becomes one of its portals: you see the other side live and walk straight through. The top and bottom of the loop become world-wide portals too. Without it the mod draws its own view through doors and seams. Note that Immersive Portals needs Cloth Config installed.

title: Shaders, Iris, Sodium
text: Works with Sodium and Iris , with shader packs on. The view through a door and the edge of the loop are painted into a texture first, so a shader pack draws them like any block.

title: Tested with
text: Immersive Portals, Sable, Sodium, Iris, Distant Horizons, Create, JEI, Jade, ModernFix, Curios. Better Minecraft 5 (tested on its server pack). Other dimension mods The Remembering blocks Nether and End portals inside it. Portals from other mods may also not behave inside; doors are the way in and out.

title: Servers
text: Install the mod on the server and every client. No other mods needed. Dedicated servers do not kick players for "flying" on the long falls inside (a pit, the geometry, the loop). Only up to 8 chunks are sent to a player inside The Remembering by default ( remembering.viewDistance ): the fog hides anything further, and every chunk there is a 1392-block column. Tune or switch off thin spots, build copying, the Keeper, Still Lifes, insanity and the leave cooldown in backrooms-server.toml . Players can use /backrooms leave ; ops have /backrooms pull , keeper , quiet and loud and more ( Commands ).

title: Updating from 2.0.0
text: The old dimension (The Complex) is replaced. Its folder is moved to dimensions/backrooms/the_complex_2.0_backup , nothing is deleted. Players saved inside it are brought back to the overworld with a message. Overworld, items and Memarium carry over. Old iron-frame portals no longer open.

title: Reporting bugs
text: Report bugs and mod conflicts on the mod's CurseForge page or its Discord.

title: Getting In
text: Home » Start » Getting In There are two ways in: a door of Reinforced Iron you power with redstone, and the thin spots that open up in the world after the first door does.

title: Getting In
text: A powered Reinforced Iron door, open, with the lever that powers it. An older, weathered frame stands beside it.

title: Reinforced Iron
text: Reinforced Iron is the door frame block. Craft it from 4 iron ingots, 4 copper ingots and a block of iron ( recipe ); the recipe makes one block. You also find four of it in the chest beside the broken machine in every Buried Works , and iron, copper and redstone turn up in The Remembering's chests, barrels and Vivid mobs, so nobody is ever stuck inside without a way to build a door. Mine it with an iron pickaxe or better. It never drops itself: it breaks into 2 iron ingots, 2 copper ingots and sometimes the block of iron. It weathers like vanilla copper: exposed, weathered, oxidized. Honeycom

title: Building a door
text: Build a closed frame of Reinforced Iron around an empty opening, like a Nether portal frame. Any shape works, with an opening up to 21 by 21. The frame must be unbroken; the corners are up to you, like a Nether portal's. Give any block of the frame a redstone signal: a lever, a button, a Block of Redstone beside it, a redstone torch. The door kindles for 2.5 seconds : light gathers round the inside of the frame and flickers on like a fluorescent tube on redstone power, with a rising power-up sound, then it opens with a deep boom. Cut the power and the door closes again. Break the frame and it

title: Crossing
text: Walk into the open door and you are on the other side on the next tick, with no loading screen: the game holds its last picture until the new room has drawn. Each time an overworld door opens, the 25 by 25 room around it is copied into The Remembering at the same coordinates, lifted a little so its floor meets one of the dimension's floors, and a twin door opens there. Walk through and the room is the same room. Walk out of it and it isn't. Through the door: the same machine hall, copied. A few steps out of the copy, the office floors begin. The twin door inside The Remembering stays open on i

title: Doors in every dimension
text: Doors work in every dimension, both ways: A door in the overworld opens into the overworld floors of The Remembering at the same x, y and z. A door in the Nether opens into The Remembering's Nether floors at the same spot. A door in the End opens into its End floors. A door built inside The Remembering opens back out onto the world its level remembers: the overworld from the overworld floors, the real Nether from the Nether floors, the real End from the End floors. No other portals work inside Nether portals cannot be lit or used inside The Remembering, and neither can End portals. Only its do

title: Thin spots
text: Once the first door in a world opens, the overworld starts wearing thin. Thin spots are patches of ground in the Overworld, Nether and End that look like the block they replaced and hold no weight. They show only as a slightly darker top with a faint dark rim, so the patch looks like a shallow dip. Step onto one and you drop through into The Remembering at the same spot, with the Distorted effect: a blurred, fogged view for a while. A thin spot is at least a plus of five blocks. title: Getting out
text: Walk back through any open door. Build your own door inside: it opens onto the world that level remembers. Type /backrooms leave : anyone can, with a cooldown (10 minutes by default; ops have none). It takes you to the overworld, by the door you came in through if there is one. Die: you respawn at your spawn point as usual, unless you set your spawn at a charged Stand-In inside. Respawn inside Going in for a long trip? title: Home
text: A standalone NeoForge mod that adds The Remembering : a copy of your own world, cut into endless office floors, with something inside that can't decide what it is. The builders who made the ancient cities and the strongholds tried one last fix: a machine that reaches into the world's memory of itself. It woke the memory instead. The story is never told in text. You learn it by playing: by the places, the objects, the sounds and the rules of the place. This wiki is the other way round: it tells you everything plainly. If you would rather find things out for yourself, stop at Getting started .

title: What is in the mod
text: The Remembering , a new dimension: your world at the same coordinates, remembered floor upon floor, from overworld floors down through Nether and End floors to a geometric level, all one vertical loop. Reinforced Iron and the Gateway : a door frame of any shape that opens when it gets a redstone signal. Doors work in every dimension, both ways. The Keeper , the one hunter inside. It stalks, drags you away, and can only be fought once you build it a body. Vivid mobs, Hollow mobs and Still Lifes : mobs and players remembered wrong. title: Updating from 2.0.0
text: This update replaces the old dimension 3.0.0 removes the old Backrooms dimension (The Complex) and starts it fresh as The Remembering. Your world still loads, and your overworld, items and Memarium carry over. Anyone who logged out inside the old dimension comes back to the overworld with a message. title: Insanity
text: Home » The dimension » Insanity The Remembering wears on you. The insanity meter rises the longer you stay inside, and it is only ever calm in a refuge.

title: Insanity
text: High insanity: the insanity bubbles are mostly gone and dark veins close in round the edge of the screen.

title: The meter
text: Every player has an insanity meter from 0 to 1. It is shown as a row of dark insanity bubbles above the hunger bar (stacked above the air bubbles underwater) that burst one by one as it rises. Where you are What the meter does Inside The Remembering, the first 90 seconds Nothing: a grace period. Inside The Remembering after that Rises from empty to full in about 8 minutes . In a refuge or remembered room, or within a few blocks of a Gateway Falls slowly, from full to empty in about a minute. Anywhere outside The Remembering Falls fast, from full to empty in about 15 seconds. Insanity is kept w

The fog starts turning black and closes in over about ten seconds. 0.8 Nausea. 0.92 Short random teleports: you blink 6 to 30 blocks away in a burst of black. title: Settled Heart
text: Settled Heart Dropped by the Keeper when he is beaten, one for everyone in the fight, even a fighter who never landed a hit. The middle of the Memento and Snapshot recipes. Each heart is kept for its own fighter while they are still around (online, in The Remembering and within 64 blocks), for up to a minute, so whoever stands on the drop can't take everyone's. A heart whose fighter left or went far off is anyone's after 3 seconds. Hearts never come out inside or behind a wall. See Beating him .

title: Memento
text: Memento Give it your inventory, and take it back later. Whatever you carry then is left behind in The Remembering. Use an empty Memento: it costs one Memarium Ingot and stores everything you carry, armor included. Use it again to get it all back. Whatever you were carrying at that moment is dropped in The Remembering, at the same spot (or the nearest floor). The advancement is A Fair Trade . Crafted from a compass, a Settled Heart and an ender pearl in a row ( recipe ). Never found in chests.

title: Snapshot
text: Snapshot Remember a build, and put back whatever goes missing. It fades with time. Sneak and use it on two opposite corners to save a build, up to 16 by 16 by 16. Later, use it on any block there to put back what is missing. It takes the blocks from your inventory and one Memarium Ingot, and the Snapshot is used up. It only works in the dimension it was taken in. After the first in-game day it starts to fade: more and more of what it puts back comes back plainer, or not at all. Wash it clean in a water cauldron. The advancement is Hold Still . Crafted from a map, a Settled Heart and an ender p

title: Memory Anchor
text: Memory Anchor While it has a redstone signal, no thin spot forms anywhere in the world, and the ones out there close back into the blocks they replaced. Its crystal turns while powered. Memarium Ingots in the corners, Blocks of Redstone on the edges and an End Crystal in the middle ( recipe ). It weathers like copper; wax it to keep its look, and a mined anchor keeps its stage and wax. Powering one gives Hold On .

title: Stand-In
text: Stand-In The Remembering's respawn anchor. Charge it with Raw Memarium, set your spawn, and it keeps your likeness. Raw Memarium charges it, up to 4. Its light and its comparator signal climb with the charge, like a respawn anchor's. Use it with a charge in it: your respawn point is set there and the advancement is Someone to Come Back To . Your head, washed grey, turns inside the cage. Empty, it is silent and does nothing. Every respawn at it spends one charge. You come back standing beside it. With no charge left, or if it is gone, you go back to world spawn. Only in The Remembering. Anywher

title: The Keeper
text: Home » What lives there » The Keeper There is one hunter in The Remembering. It can't settle on a shape. The longer you stay, the more things it becomes, and the angrier it gets.

title: The Keeper
text: The Keeper, far off between the pillars. The Keeper, close.

title: The hunter
text: There is one Keeper per world. It is the world trying to remember every mob and every thing at once, unable to settle on one shape: the builders' last monster. Its body keeps changing, and the longer you stay inside, the more things it becomes. It hunts the player who has spent the most time inside, once that player has been in for 10 minutes on a visit. It only comes closer while you are not looking . It stalks from cover: it waits right beside a wall, a door jamb or a pillar where you can't see it, often peeking out with just the side of its face or an arm past the corner, and moves on only

title: Anger
text: Its anger comes from your total time inside , across every visit: Anger Total time inside 0 under 6 minutes 1 6 to 15 minutes 2 15 to 28 minutes 3 28 minutes or more Each time it gets angrier, the lights near you are likely to go out in a blackout . Its anger also decides how many Vivids it summons in a fight.

title: Caught
text: After stalking a while it plays its charge sound, waits, then runs at you. If it reaches you, it grabs you: 6 damage, blindness and darkness, and you are dragged away , either back to the door you came in by or two to five floors down. Then it retreats. Being caught gives the advancement Lost Your Place . Stand by a door It never drags someone standing by a Gateway. If it charges, get to an open door. It cannot be hurt Nothing hurts the Keeper while it hunts. To fight it you have to give it a shape.

title: The Shape: pinning it
text: You cannot beat the Keeper as it is. Build it a body and it has to take that shape. The Shape painting by The Builders, which hangs in the Buried Works, shows how. Get a Still Life Head by taking a Still Life apart. Inside The Remembering, build a T of five Blocks of Memarium : two stacked in a column, with three across the top (like an iron golem's body). Place the Still Life Head on the middle of the top row, last. The Shape: a Still Life Head on a T of five Blocks of Memarium, built inside The Remembering. The Shape painting, by The Builders: how the body is built. Building it gives the adv

title: His arrival
text: He does not appear on the spot. The Shape keeps standing, and he comes to it: He notices. For a few seconds there is nothing but sparks on the Memarium, and his sound, far off. He arrives 8 to 12 blocks away, out of sight, and the lights go out. He walks up to the Shape. Nothing can touch him now: hits just bounce off. He stands over the statue for about eleven seconds while he forms, like the Wither: the boss bar fills, yellow cracks open, frames rise round him and he grows. The fog turns black round you. He smashes the Shape. A deep boom: the walls next to him shatter, everyone within 10 blo

title: The fight
text: The pinned Keeper, boss bar up. Health 300 (150 hearts), armor 8, never knocked back Melee 12 damage up close Slam Every 11 to 15 seconds when you are within about 4 blocks: 6 damage and a hard push to everyone within 5 blocks Speed He runs a little faster than a sprinting player He fights wherever you go, up to 64 blocks away. Where he cannot walk to you (a low doorway, a pillar), he shifts beside you within a second. He knows when you run : three seconds of sprinting away and he beams you, or steps in front of you. At two thirds and one third of his health he summons Vivids : one plus his an

title: The beam: rewind and steal
text: From range (9 to about 22 blocks, or from 5 where he can't walk to you) he charges a beam like the Warden's sonic boom: 1.7 seconds, then a line of doorways runs from his face to you. The aim locks half a second before the shot , so sidestep or duck behind something. Rewind (most beams): you glide back along the way you came, the last 5 seconds played backwards, the picture drained of colour and torn. You end up exactly where you were five seconds ago. Steal (about one beam in six): the item in your hand is pulled out and drawn along the beam to his face. You can catch it on the way. If it rea

title: The rearrange
text: Thirty seconds into the fight, and then every 45 to 60 seconds, he moves the walls . Every wall of the floor within 50 blocks of him lifts, slides and drops into a new plan of the floor, rippling out from him. It does no damage, but the way you knew is gone. Pits, stairs, the ramp, refuges, structures, door rooms, your own blocks and any cell with somebody in it are left alone.

title: Eating the walls
text: Hurt (below 90% health), every 25 to 45 seconds he pulls up to eight wall blocks within 8 blocks into himself, and each one mends 5 health . Fighting in open floor, away from the walls, gives him less to eat.

title: If you die or leave
text: Only one Keeper ever exists. He is never saved with a chunk: when everyone leaves, he is gone from the world. Come back within 64 blocks of the fight within 10 minutes and he is standing there exactly as you left him, with the health he had. Nobody comes back for 10 minutes and the fight is abandoned: he is no longer pinned, and later goes back to stalking with his anger. He was not beaten, so there is no quiet period.

title: Beating him
text: Beaten, he recoils, holds still, sinks to his knees and crumbles into his own face, farthest pieces first, like the Ender Dragon dissolving. Everyone in the fight gets a Settled Heart , even someone who never landed a hit. Each heart is kept for its own fighter while they are still around, for up to a minute; one whose fighter left or went far off is anyone's after 3 seconds. Hearts never come out inside or behind a wall. Beating him gives the challenge You Can't Kill a Memory . A stolen item still in his face comes back out. Then The Remembering is quiet : no Keeper for 40 minutes by default

title: Hiding from him
text: Leggings with Stillness hide you while you stand still or crouch: he only notices you within 20, 14 or 8 blocks (levels I, II, III). Refuges and doors do not stop him, but he never drags you away from beside a Gateway. Ops can make him leave with /backrooms quiet , or turn him off in the config with keeper.enabled = false .

title: Mobs
text: Home » What lives there » Mobs Everything that lives in The Remembering is something it remembered wrong.

title: Vivid mobs
text: Vivids are hostile mobs remembered wrong. They only come out when the lights go out : they spawn in The Remembering during a blackout , and any zombie, skeleton, creeper, spider, ghast or phantom that wanders in becomes one. Each one is misremembered as it spawns: two times in three it is bigger and tougher than the real mob, otherwise smaller and weaker. Each kind has four bodies, made from the real mob's own model and skin cut up and put back together wrong. Their voices are the vanilla sounds, reworked and echoing, and kept low: they call about every 12 seconds, half as often as the real mo

title: Vivid flyers
text: Two Vivids fly. They turn up anywhere in The Remembering with enough open air to fly in, at the same rate at every depth, so you meet most of them in the geometric level (the gyroid halls and the Menger lattice), where the air is: The Vivid Ghast cruises low, 4 to 8 blocks over the ground. Every 8 to 15 seconds it glides down beside a player near it, hangs there for 2 to 3 seconds within sword reach, then climbs back. It shoots wind charges, only from cruise height. Bodies: cluster, melted, split, bearded. Drops ghast tears and gunpowder; killed by a player, a 5% chance of the music disc Day O

title: Hollow mobs
text: Hollows are animals remembered as statues : the Hollow Cow, Hollow Sheep, Hollow Pig, Hollow Chicken and Hollow Villager. They have no AI, never move and shatter when hit. They stand in small herds of one to three across the floors, and any cow, sheep, pig, chicken, villager or wandering trader that enters The Remembering becomes one. Each kind has four bodies too. Hollows: a cow, a sheep and a pig, grey and still. A Hollow Villager.

title: Still Lifes
text: A Still Life is a copy of a player who has been inside, wearing their skin. They only move while nobody is looking at them. Every two minutes there is a one in four chance a Still Life appears near each player inside who has none within 96 blocks. They copy how a player plays too. Players who kill animals and villagers or hit other players are remembered as violent, and their Still Lifes attack. Every hit or interaction takes a limb off. The last one drops a Still Life Head wearing the copied player's skin, and gives the advancement Still Life . You need a Still Life Head to pin the Keeper . S

title: Refuges
text: Home » The dimension » Refuges Not everything in The Remembering wants you lost. Some rooms are places to breathe.

title: Refuges
text: Refuges are safe rooms: fifteen by fifteen blocks, yellow-carpeted, lit, furnished, with chests. Inside one your insanity falls instead of rising. There are five kinds: the lounge , the kitchen , the workshop , the garden and the storage room. A refuge. Another refuge, its doorways open to the floor round it. A storage refuge: chests and barrels on a yellow floor. Every floor from the top of the overworld floors down through the End floors has at least one guaranteed refuge in every 256 by 256 region . More refuges turn up in groups on the overworld, Nether and End floors, stacked three floors

title: Remembered rooms
text: Remembered rooms turn up on many floors. Each remembers one part of the game, with one detail wrong: Floors Rooms Overworld floors The first night, the farm, the mine, the village square, the enchanting room, the seabed Nether floors The Nether portal, the fortress crossing End floors The End portal room, the dragon's perch The first night The enchanting room The village square The seabed The Nether portal The fortress crossing The End portal room A misremembered place, hanging over a pit.

title: Misremembered places
text: Misremembered places are chambers that hold a whole vanilla structure, loaded from the game itself and remembered wrong: blocks swapped for slabs, parts twisted, pieces missing, some Memarium, all water and lava drained. Large ones hold bigger structures; the Nether and End floors have their own. The vanilla blocks inside are not copies: they break and drop like normal blocks. The first chest you open in one sometimes makes a quiet mob sound. /backrooms locatepoi finds the nearest misremembered place or remembered room.

title: What is in the chests
text: Room chests and barrels in The Remembering hold food, light, paper and string, iron and copper ingots, ladders and the odd iron tool. Rarer finds: An enchanted book with one of the four Remembering enchantments : Keeping, Stillness, Slow Fall or Curse of Fading. Apart from the odd enchanted book in a Buried Works archive, they are found nowhere else. A Potion of Sanity, or a Splash Potion of Insanity. Raw Memarium, a disc fragment. A Remembered Upgrade template: 9% per chest in remembered rooms and in the refuges that come in groups. Iron, a block of iron, copper, redstone, levers and redstone

title: Rules of the dimension
text: Home » The dimension » Rules of the dimension The Remembering is not built of real blocks. It has its own rules, and learning them is most of surviving there.

title: Everything is a copy
text: Almost every block The Remembering generates is a copy . Copies follow their own rules: Any tool breaks them, but only Memarium tools break them at normal speed. Anything else gets a hidden Mining Fatigue II and works at about a tenth of the speed. Copies drop nothing when broken. Explosions do not break copies. Blocks you place there yourself are not copies: they break and drop normally, like anywhere else. So do Memarium ore and the vanilla pieces inside misremembered places . Nether portals and End portals cannot be lit or used inside. Only doors work.

title: Memarium
text: The Remembering never remembers ore, because the builders took it all. Where ore was, it leaves a hole, and now and then, as a whole vein, it fills it with Memarium , the only metal it makes. Memarium ore comes in four kinds: Memarium Ore , Deepslate Memarium Ore , Nether Memarium Ore and End Memarium Ore . It drops Raw Memarium (or the ore with Silk Touch). Smelt or blast it into a Memarium Ingot . Veins are rare and there is never a lone block of it. In the geometric level they sit in thick floors.

title: Memarium tools and drops
text: Memarium tools are diamond tools upgraded at a smithing table with a Remembered Upgrade and a Memarium Ingot ( recipes ). They are the key to The Remembering, not a better pickaxe: Inside, they are the only tools that cut copies at full speed. What they cut breaks into nothing, almost always. Now and then a block drops: the rarer the block, the rarer the drop. A dirt block drops one time in five, a diamond block one time in a thousand. Settled blocks and Settled Lichen always drop. Servers can turn the chance up or down with memariumDropMultiplier in the config . Outside The Remembering, Memar

title: Copies of your builds
text: The Remembering copies what players build. Blocks you place or break in the overworld show up at the same x, y and z in The Remembering, a little wrong, while nobody there is looking: Some of the copied blocks are lost, and some are remembered as a plainer version of themselves. Thin blocks, blocks with contents (chests, furnaces), door rooms, floors and lamps are left alone. Finding one of your own builds in there gives the advancement It's Copying Me . Server owners can turn it off with remembering.copyBuilds . A house built in the overworld, remembered in The Remembering at the same spot.

title: Mobs that wander in
text: Vanilla mobs that enter The Remembering are remembered wrong as soon as they arrive: hostile mobs turn into Vivids , animals and villagers into Hollow statues. Some mobs are refused and simply do not come in.

title: Insanity
text: The longer you stay inside, the more your mind goes. It has its own page: Insanity .

title: Death and leaving
text: Dying inside: you respawn at your spawn point, and your insanity is cleared. Beds and respawn anchors don't work in there; they blow up, like a bed in the Nether. Items enchanted with Keeping stay with you through death. Items with Curse of Fading vanish when their holder leaves The Remembering. /backrooms leave takes you out, with a cooldown.

title: Respawning inside: the Stand-In
text: Beds and respawn anchors don't work in The Remembering. The Stand-In does the job instead: a copper cage that holds a grey copy of your head. Charge it with Raw Memarium , one charge each, up to 4. Use it with a charge in it and your respawn point is set there. Your head appears in the cage, washed grey, and turns slowly while it still has charge. Empty, it does nothing at all: no message, no spawn. Each time you respawn at it, one charge is used. With none left you go back to world spawn. Outside The Remembering it does nothing: "It doesn't remember this place." Its copper weathers like a cop

title: The Remembering
text: Home » The dimension » The Remembering It is your world, at the same coordinates, remembered floor upon floor. It gets some of it wrong.

title: The Remembering
text: An overworld floor: plain office rooms, doorways and lamps.

title: One loop, 1392 blocks tall
text: The Remembering ( backrooms:the_remembering ) runs from y 319 down to y -1072 . It is your world at the same x and z, and it is one loop: fall out of the bottom and you come out at the top; build or fly out of the top and you come out at the bottom. There are no loading screens anywhere inside. y 319 to y -64 Overworld floors Your overworld, cut into office floors at its own height: your hills, trees and villages poke through the walls above ground, rooms are carved out of remembered stone and deepslate below. Lamps: 93% lit. y -65 to y -192 Nether floors Copies of the real Nether, fortresses

title: The building
text: The floors are laid on a 7-block grid of cells, and every stretch of floor is a mix of zones: rooms, cubicles, long halls running east-west or north-south, big rooms, pillar fields and empty open floor. Walls between cells can be open, solid, a doorway or a half-height wall. It never remembers ore . Where ore was there is a hole, and now and then, as a whole vein, Memarium . Your builds turn up in it, a little wrong, when nobody is looking. So does what you break, slowly. See Rules . It changes only when nobody is looking. The deeper you go, the more it gets wrong.

title: Floor styles
text: Not every floor is the same building. Every few thousand blocks a floor turns into another kind of place, blending over about 200 blocks, and the floors above and below are different again. Some of every floor stays the classic office. Style What it is Classic The office as it always was. About half of every floor. Pillar Field Open floor and pillars every 7 blocks, as far as the fog lets you see. Long Halls Halls 33 blocks long with a yellow carpet down the middle and blind corners. Maze One-cell passages, no rooms, no doors. Tall Rooms Two floors merged into ten-block-high rooms, lamps on th

title: Pits, shafts, stairs and the ramp
text: Pits are wide square holes through many floors. Most regions of about 192 by 192 blocks hold one. About a quarter of them go the whole way round the loop; the rest stop at a floor part way down. /backrooms locate pit finds the nearest one that goes all the way. Shafts (2 by 2) and stair cells link neighbouring floors everywhere. In about half of all 320-block regions a long ramp , 96 blocks long and 3 wide, cuts down through the floors. Stairs lead down from the End's lowest floor into the geometric level. You can always dig or build your own way up or down. Across a pit Down a pit that goes a

title: The geometric level
text: Under the End floors the building gives up. The geometric level runs from y -305 to the bottom at y -1072: Forgetting floors (the first 320 blocks): office floors of varying height being eaten away by the math. The gyroid halls are an endless curved surface of stepped blocks you walk, climb and fall through. Gravity is strange in places. Halfway down, the gyroid morphs into the Menger lattice , a giant stepped cube lattice that runs to the bottom. Over the last 120 blocks the cubes shrink, so none of them touches the loop. In the math you also meet swallowed offices (whole office blocks half e

title: Memories and landmarks
text: Memories hang in pockets of the geometry: 20 famous places and builds, each remembered as a floating island (11 of the mod's own and 9 from vanilla's structures). Landmarks are bigger: an end city ship and two giant ruined portals. /backrooms locate memory finds the nearest memory once you are in the geometric level. A memory hanging in the gyroid. Another memory: a remembered building on its own island. Here and there in the geometry the blocks have an old look : pockets of Old Stone, Old Cobblestone, Old Bricks and 26 other "old" blocks. They use the pre-1.14 textures from your own copy of t

title: The seams
text: At the top and bottom of the loop you can look through: within about 96 blocks of a seam you see the other end of the loop through the haze, never the void. With Immersive Portals installed, the seams become real world-wide portals. Fall out of the bottom (y -1071) and you come out at the top, same x, z, speed and facing. Rise into the top (y 319, the top floor has no ceiling) and you come out at the bottom. Mobs and items cross the seams too. Nothing can stand on a seam: anything touching or pressing into one goes through at once. Climb a ladder up into the top seam and you come out at the bo

title: Lamps, flicker and blackouts
text: The ceilings are lit by Stuck, Flickering and Burnt-Out Lamps : redstone lamps that stay lit, flicker or stay dark without any power. The lower the floor, the more of them are dark. Flickering lamps only flicker near players, a few bursts a minute. In a blackout every lamp around you goes out at once, for 3 to 45 seconds, then comes back in a wave. The fog closes in to about 18 blocks. A blackout often comes when the Keeper gets angrier, and now and then one comes below the End. Vivid mobs on the ground only spawn during a blackout. Vivid ghasts and phantoms can turn up at any time where there

title: Settled patches
text: Rarely, part of a floor has gone the Keeper's brown-black: settled . In a settled spot, area or room the birch walls, mushroom and mud floors, the cut sandstone ceiling and the lamps are their settled versions , the settled lamps dim and flickering. At the edges the office goes black a block at a time, and Settled Lichen creeps over the floor and up the walls round them. Refuges and structures are never settled. title: The rooms it remembers
text: The Remembering also builds rooms of its own on many floors: refuges where your insanity falls, remembered rooms that each remember one part of the game with one detail wrong, and misremembered places that hold a whole vanilla structure, glitched. They have their own page: Refuges .
